S45.01.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account on a plan that includes image generation, and a photo in the phone library or simulator; the image-generation rows only appear in AGI Cloud mode
S45.01.note: The code reads the attached photo as the source to edit only when the chat is in image mode; I did not confirm the composer preview or send button wording on a device. The send button has no visible text label in the code (testID chat.composer.send).
steps: Sign in and open a chat in AGI Cloud mode.
Tap the + button labelled Add to chat next to the message box.
Tap Create image in the sheet so the chat is in image mode.
Tap Photos in the top row of the sheet and choose a photo from your library.
Type a short prompt and tap send.
Check the sent message shows your photo and that the reply is an image made from it, as Expected says.
S45.01.where: Add to chat (+ button at the left of the chat composer) > Photos > pick a photo; the photo then shows as an attachment in the composer, with Create image on in the same sheet

S45.03.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account on a plan that includes image generation, and a photo to edit
S45.03.note: The app refuses to edit when the selected image model cannot use a reference (message: This model uses text only. Pick an editing model to edit a photo.); the tester should check the model choice in the Image model list first. Whether the sheet closes after Create image is not confirmed in code.
steps: Open a chat in AGI Cloud mode and tap the + button labelled Add to chat.
Tap Create image, then tap Photos and choose a photo.
Close the sheet and type a change in the message box, for example a colour or object change.
Compare the returned image with the photo: the requested change should appear while the rest stays similar, as Expected says.
S45.03.where: Add to chat (+) > Create image, then type the change in the message box and send, with a photo attached through Photos

labels.text: Attach up to 4 photos. The first is edited; the rest guide it.

S45.22.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account on a plan that includes image generation, and two photos in the phone library or simulator
S45.22.note: Code allows the first photo plus up to 3 more (MANAGED_MEDIA_MAX_IMAGE_REFERENCES = 3 in packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts); the guide photos are sent only with an editing model. Whether the reference is carried over visibly depends on the model, not checked here.
steps: Open a chat in AGI Cloud mode and tap the + button labelled Add to chat.
Tap Create image, then tap Photos and choose a first photo; tap Photos again to add a second photo for reference.
Read the hint Attach up to 4 photos. The first is edited; the rest guide it.
Type a prompt that says what to keep from the second photo, such as its subject, layout or style, and tap send.
Compare the result with the reference photo: subject, layout or style from the reference should carry over, as Expected says.
S45.22.where: Add to chat (+) > Create image > Photos (add up to 4 photos; the hint reads Attach up to 4 photos. The first is edited; the rest guide it.), then type a prompt and send

S45.31.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account on a plan that includes image generation, and a photo to edit
S45.31.note: The code attaches the source photo to the request message before generation (runImageGenerationTurn.ts lines 253-267) and returns a new reply; no visible label for this was found, and whether the bubble shows the original next to the result on screen was not checked.
steps: Do the steps for S45.01 and send the edit request.
Look at your request message in the chat: the photo you attached should still be shown there.
Look at the reply: it should be a new image, and your original photo should not be replaced, as Expected says.
S45.31.where: No control of its own: the photo you sent for an edit is attached to your request message in the chat, and the new image is a separate reply
